one_liner: Trace, profile, and optimize the five-phase RL rollout-to-gradient loop and its staleness tradeoffs.

key_terms.definition: How many optimizer steps old the weights were when they generated the rollouts now being trained on; the dial between throughput and on-policyness.
Per-token ratio pi_theta/pi_behavior correcting for the mismatch between the training policy and the (possibly older) policy that generated the data.
PPO/GRPO loss that clips the importance ratio to a bounded range, limiting the gradient contribution of tokens that have drifted off-policy.
On-policy means the training data was generated by the exact current policy weights; off-policy means it came from older or different weights.
A purpose-built inference server (vLLM, SGLang) used for the generation phase instead of naive `model.generate`, exploiting batching and cache-sharing tricks.
Scheduling technique where a finished sequence's slot is immediately refilled by a waiting sequence, avoiding idle time from static batch padding.
KV-cache management scheme storing cache entries in non-contiguous pages allocated on demand rather than pre-padded to max length, enabling larger effective batches.
Computing the KV cache for a shared prompt prefix once and reusing it across all G group completions sampled from that prompt.
Fraction of a GPU's peak FLOP/s actually achieved by a workload; training runs at 40-55% MFU while memory-bound decode collapses to a few percent.
Copying newly trained policy weights into the (possibly separate-process) inference engine before or during the next rollout, the loop's Phase 5.
Binary mask marking generated response tokens (1) versus prompt/padding tokens (0), used so loss, advantages, and KL are computed only on chosen tokens.
Diagnostic metric: the share of tokens whose importance ratio left the clip range, indicating how far training has drifted off-policy.

prerequisites: FSDP or other distributed training basics
